For each finalist pair, label the relation of the extra content, then apply one fixed direction:
 - UP (choose the longer option). The extra clause is a same-kind qualitative upgrade on an object the stem already names: iff over one-way; the full limit object (metric or equation included) over parameter-only convergence; 'fully' over plain; a standard companion of the same inequality (strict log-concavity off the plateau); a Moreover whose hypothesis is stated inside the option and whose conclusion is a one-line consequence.

It may quantify over objects the stem fixed (for all m when the stem fixes k). It may be a gloss swapping an explicit threshold for a simpler one. It may delete or relax a hypothesis.
 - REJECT. The option is a tautology, a restatement of the stem's own hypothesis (for example, 'invariant iff constant', or 'no nonsolvable group' when the stem assumes solvability), or has a tail of 'only', 'need not', or 'non-uniform'. Reject it even when it looks safe.
 - If the options are nested and neither label applies, take the one in the stem's own vocabulary.

Every surviving rule needs a named trigger and one direction. Keep verbatim: the atomic-clause split, the hub test, and the first two sentences of the final sanity pass.

5. Rank edits. Up: a visible ritual plus table that replaces several scattered paragraphs and shortens the file. Down: anything that only restates an existing rule, adds an item tied to one task, or adds a prefer-stronger or prefer-plainer rule with no trigger.
